title: Attribute Routing
description: Master attribute routing for API endpoints.

data.text: Attribute routing gives you precise control over your API URLs using attributes on controllers and actions.
Route tokens are placeholders inside a route pattern that are replaced at runtime. The most common token is `[controller]`, which is replaced with the controller name without the `Controller` suffix.

data.title: Tokens

data.text: Each HTTP method has a dedicated attribute. Using these attributes makes your routes self-documenting and aligns with REST conventions.

data.title: RESTful URLs
data.text: Use nouns for resources (/users, /products), not verbs. HTTP methods indicate the action.

data.title: Design a RESTful Route
data.description: Create attribute routes for a Product resource following REST conventions.
steps: Add a [Route("api/[controller]")] attribute to the controller
data.expectedOutcome: A controller with six RESTful endpoints: GET /api/products, GET /api/products/{id}, POST /api/products, PUT /api/products/{id}, DELETE /api/products/{id}.

items.text: Use [Route] on the controller for the base path
Apply HTTP method attributes to each action
Use nouns, not verbs, in resource paths
Use route tokens to avoid hardcoding names
items.hint: Keeps routes flexible when renaming controllers.

data.title: Key Takeaways
data.takeaway: Attribute routing creates clean API URLs.
